final_draft.answer: No. A live check of our GitHub organisation (harborlight) on 2026-11-16 found that the organisation does not require two-factor sign-in for its members.
final_draft.note: Please review before sending: the approved answer and the live setting disagree. The approved answer (answer:aff37ead-9867-4840-b13d-d7daa09108a3, owner security@harborlight.example, valid until 2027-11-16) says the harborlight GitHub organisation requires two-factor sign-in for all members. But the live check at 2026-11-16T16:58:53Z found it is not required (two_factor_required: false). I didn't reuse the approved wording because the live check shows it is currently untrue. The draft answer is based only on the live check. The Access Control Policy (section 4.2) requires all workforce members to use a second factor, so the GitHub setting appears to break that policy. The control owner should decide whether to turn on the GitHub organisation's two-factor requirement before this answer goes out, and should update or retire the approved answer either way. Also, the employee MFA answer covers identity-provider accounts, not the GitHub organisation's own setting, so it doesn't answer this question.
